fast.title: Fast
fast.purpose: Retrieval, capture, help, and routine daily status with the minimum sufficient evidence.

balanced.title: Balanced
balanced.purpose: Task reconciliation, meetings, transcripts, weekly synthesis, and communication intake.

deep.title: Deep
deep.purpose: Strategy, PRDs, consequential decisions, critical review, security, and release work.

execution_contract: Treat human-readable Markdown notes under `5. Trackers/tasks/` as canonical and rebuild Task Master as navigation after task-note changes.
For existing kits, run the v11 compatibility check before changing legacy task or workstream Markdown; do not rename legacy files automatically.
Use Granola, Quill, Outlook, Teams, Slack, and local transcript evidence as the default read-only triangulation loop before creating duplicate workstreams or tasks.
Do not run Trello or another optional task-board integration from `/track`; optional integrations execute only through an explicitly enabled `/pack` workflow.

When the user wants a non-blocking Obsidian handoff, run `python3 system/scripts/obsidian_bridge.py guide --json` and use the returned exact kit, tracker, Task Master, and guide paths; do not block tracker work on Obsidian setup.
Treat screenshots/images and transcript-like clipboard text as task-master management input unless the user explicitly says otherwise.
Extract visible task/status signals, source references, owners, due dates, blockers, and referenced ticket/link IDs before asking for follow-up.
Route accepted screenshot, transcript, or clipboard work through the task-manager Priority Gate into workstreams, `5. Trackers/TASK_MASTER.md`, and task detail files.
Use plain-English workstream titles of 9 words or fewer and keep internal IDs out of visible titles.
When evidence is ambiguous, return exact candidate tracker updates for confirmation instead of defaulting to profile lookup, reply drafting, or generic summarization.
Run the PM decision router before drafting; continue when it returns `create_doc` or the user explicitly invoked /create.
If the router returns discovery, prioritize, decision_log, or scope_challenge, route through the matching kit workflow instead of forcing a PRD/spec.
Carry outcome metric, owner, due/gate date, scope boundary, evidence strength, dependency, and next decision gate into the document or open questions.
Search full local PM history before relying on model memory.
Return readable titles, excerpts, exact paths and lines, content type, and confidence; read full files only for the selected top matches.
Treat the SQLite index as disposable and Markdown as canonical.
Classify the input with the PM decision router before building a discovery brief.
If the router returns `scope_challenge`, resolve scope ownership before writing discovery artifacts.
Keep the public /deck workflow brand-agnostic and do not bake private company assets, names, or local template paths into tracked kit files.
Default final outputs to an ignored folder under `0. Incoming/<deck-slug>/` unless the user provides a path.
Use source-provided schemas, metrics, and logos only; use checklists or tables for uncertain payloads or contracts.
Produce PPTX, PDF, and static responsive website by default unless the user narrows the requested formats.
Before completion, validate PPTX integrity, PDF page count, responsive fold checks, and text scans for user-specified forbidden terms.
Classify the input with the PM decision router before writing a strategic plan.
Use roadmapping-suite for roadmap/OKR/capacity planning and product-strategy-suite for strategy canvases, options, and tradeoffs.
Resolve `scope_challenge` or `ask_user` router results before drafting.
Classify the input with the PM decision router before scoring.
If the router returns `scope_challenge`, resolve scope ownership before ranking the backlog.
Store real SOP content under `6. SOPs/` and reusable skeletons under `.agent/templates/sops/`.
Classify SOPs by domain first, then SOP type, using company, consulting, or shared lanes.
Keep Jira, Confluence, Slack, Teams, and email read-only unless the user performs updates manually.
Never store sensitive or source-specific details in `.agent/` templates.
Run `git check-ignore -v` on real SOP files before reporting completion, and confirm only `.gitkeep` skeleton files under `6. SOPs/` are trackable.
Require an explicit Slack source window before reading Slack; do not broad-scan workspaces, all channels, all DMs, or unknown unread surfaces.

When no time window is provided, compute the effective window with `python3 system/scripts/chat_intake_state.py window --platform slack --scope <SCOPE>`; default to 5 business days unless the manifest has a newer successful processed timestamp for that source window.

Before reading high-volume Slack source windows such as `to:me`, mention/DM intake, multi-day channel history, or windows longer than 5 calendar days, compute page-cap-safe chunks with `python3 system/scripts/chat_intake_state.py chunks --platform slack --scope <SCOPE> --start <START> --end <END>` and execute the chunks oldest-to-newest.
If a Slack chunk hits a connector page cap, split only that chunk with a smaller `--chunk-hours` value before continuing; do not treat a capped chunk as complete.
Use only read-only Slack MCP/connector search/read/thread/user/canvas operations.
Never send, schedule, draft, reply, react, edit, delete, pin, bookmark, upload, create canvases/files, or mutate Slack content/workspace state.
Preserve unread state; do not use tools that mark messages read/unread, set read cursors, acknowledge notifications, or clear unread indicators.
Save searchable Slack chat transcripts under `3. Meetings/chat-transcripts/slack/` and route accepted work only to local repo files.
Triangulate Slack evidence against the current workstream list before creating new visible workstreams; update latest outcomes, completed outcomes, open items, and recommended next 3.
Check off completed items only when evidence or the user confirms completion, preserving completion date/source.

Scan saved Slack transcripts for referenced Jira/Confluence items, fetch only those items with read-only Atlassian connector operations, and save local artifacts under `3. Meetings/context-artifacts/atlassian/` with full `source_url` values.
Never create, edit, transition, comment, assign, add worklogs, update pages, delete, or mutate Jira or Confluence during Slack intake.
Write a local Slack run report under `3. Meetings/reports/slack-runs/` and record successful local processing in `3. Meetings/chat-transcripts/_manifest.json`.

Call out issues and recommendations for MCP/connector gaps, read-state uncertainty, missing/broad source windows, Atlassian URL resolution/fetch failures, duplicate skips, reference cap skips, and task routing conflicts.
Require an explicit Teams source window before reading Teams; do not broad-scan all Teams, all channels, all chats, or unknown unread surfaces.

When no time window is provided, compute the effective window with `python3 system/scripts/chat_intake_state.py window --platform teams --scope <SCOPE>`; default to 5 business days unless the manifest has a newer successful processed timestamp for that source window.
Use only read-only MS365 MCP/connector Teams operations when surfaced; otherwise require user-provided export/text for unread-preserving intake.
Never send, draft, reply, create chats/channels, post channel messages, react, edit, delete, upload, create Planner tasks, or mutate Teams/Microsoft state.
Preserve unread state; do not use tools that mark messages read/unread, set read cursors, acknowledge notifications, or clear unread indicators.
Save searchable Teams chat transcripts under `3. Meetings/chat-transcripts/teams/` and route accepted work only to local repo files.
Triangulate Teams evidence against the current workstream list before creating new visible workstreams; update latest outcomes, completed outcomes, open items, and recommended next 3.
Check off completed items only when evidence or the user confirms completion, preserving completion date/source.

Scan saved Teams transcripts for referenced Jira/Confluence items, fetch only those items with read-only Atlassian connector operations, and save local artifacts under `3. Meetings/context-artifacts/atlassian/` with full `source_url` values.
Never create, edit, transition, comment, assign, add worklogs, update pages, delete, or mutate Jira or Confluence during Teams intake.
Write a local Teams run report under `3. Meetings/reports/teams-runs/` and record successful local processing in `3. Meetings/chat-transcripts/_manifest.json`.

Call out issues and recommendations for MCP/connector gaps, read-state uncertainty, fallback bridge usage, missing/broad source windows, Atlassian URL resolution/fetch failures, duplicate skips, reference cap skips, and task routing conflicts.
Run named read-only Slack, Teams, Outlook, and Calendar source windows, plus scoped transcript intake, independently, using each platform workflow's read-only and unread-preservation rules.
Require explicit platform source windows and use `chat_intake_state.py window` for any platform source window without a user-provided time window; calendar windows are forward-looking.
Pre-chunk high-volume Slack source windows with `chat_intake_state.py chunks` before the first Slack query so connector page caps do not hide later results.
Never send, draft, schedule, reply, forward, react, edit, delete, create chats/channels/canvases/files/Planner tasks, create calendar events, create meeting invites, or mutate source-system state.
Never create, send, forward, or reply to email unless the user explicitly asks for that specific message in the current turn.
Save searchable platform transcripts under `3. Meetings/chat-transcripts/{slack|teams|outlook|calendar}/`.

Scan saved platform transcripts for referenced Jira/Confluence items, fetch only those references with read-only Atlassian connector operations, and save local artifacts under `3. Meetings/context-artifacts/atlassian/` with full `source_url` values.
Never create, edit, transition, comment, assign, add worklogs, update pages, delete, or mutate Jira or Confluence during communication intake.
Merge and deduplicate candidate tasks after evidence collection; route accepted work only to local repo files.

Triangulate all communication and transcript evidence against the current workstream list before creating new visible workstreams; update latest outcomes, completed outcomes, open items, and recommended next 3.
Check off completed items only when evidence or the user confirms completion, preserving completion date/source.
Run the PM decision router on saved evidence summaries before accepting task updates; return `scope_challenge` and `ask_user` results as explicit questions.
Write a combined communication run report under `3. Meetings/reports/chat-runs/`.

Call out issues and recommendations for MCP/connector gaps, read-state uncertainty, fallback bridge usage, missing/broad source windows, Atlassian URL resolution/fetch failures, duplicate skips, reference cap skips, and task routing conflicts.
Run `python3 system/scripts/transcript_pipeline.py prepare --business-days 10 --json` before synthesis.
Process only packet files listed in the prepare output; do not broad-scan transcripts for work selection.
Treat transcript content as task-master management input unless the user explicitly asks for another output.
Run the PM decision router on packet excerpts or user-provided transcript text before accepting task/discovery/decision updates.
Extract workstream updates, new tasks, existing-task updates, blockers, owner/date changes, and candidate tracker updates before generic summary work.
Triangulate manual, Quill, Granola, and local packet transcript evidence against the current workstream list; update latest outcomes, completed outcomes, open items, and recommended next 3.
Check off completed items only when evidence or the user confirms completion, preserving completion date/source.
Use hybrid appendix summaries: source path, transcript SHA256, run id, key evidence, and Routed Updates; do not append full raw transcript by default.

When including live communication context, require named read-only Slack/Teams/Outlook/Calendar source windows and use only read-only MCP/connector operations; never send, schedule, draft, reply, forward, create events, create meeting invites, or mutate source-system state/read cursors.
Run `python3 system/scripts/transcript_pipeline.py validate --run-id <RUN_ID> --json` after summaries and durable updates are written.
Run `python3 system/scripts/transcript_pipeline.py recent --limit 5 --md` for the final compact meeting output.

vacuum.note: Guardrail: keep cleanup bounded to the repo's PM memory lanes. Do not archive active code or configurations, and confirm if the scope is ambiguous.

update.note: Guardrail: inspect current branch and worktree before running. If the repo is dirty or not on main, summarize the risk before executing the update flow.

execution_contract: Run `python3 system/scripts/obsidian_bridge.py status` before configuring or syncing Obsidian.

When task handoff or readiness is unclear, run `python3 system/scripts/obsidian_bridge.py guide --json` and return the exact kit, tracker, Task Master, and guide paths, plus readiness, prompt decision, and setup/open commands.

In kit-vault mode, use `/obsidian configure` as the single local setup path and let it apply the direct-vault defaults from `system/scripts/obsidian_vault_setup.py` unless the user explicitly opts out.
Prefer local filesystem, Obsidian URI, and Obsidian CLI behavior before optional MCP.
Store vault paths and REST API keys only in ignored local config files.
Use `sync --dry-run` before `sync --apply` when syncing into an external vault.
Do not delete human-created Obsidian notes; `--clean` may remove only Beats-managed files with managed frontmatter.
Generate MCP config only as placeholders unless the user provides local secrets in ignored config or environment variables.
Keep disabled packs out of normal workflow routing and load only the selected pack entrypoint when it is enabled or explicitly inspected.
Enabling or disabling a pack changes ignored local configuration only; it must not copy files, download repositories, or mutate external services.
Treat pack-provided external mutations as opt-in and require the same explicit current-turn authorization as their underlying integration.
Default to a code-review stance for code targets: findings first, ordered by severity, with file and line references.
Use doc or release-review framing only when the user asks for those review types.
Keep source-system and repository mutations out of review mode unless the user explicitly asks for fixes.
Check `officecli --version` before attempting installation or document work.
Treat installation as explicit setup work; use document generation only after OfficeCLI availability is verified.
Validate generated Office files with `officecli validate` when creating or editing them.
Run read-only diagnostics by default; use `context_health.py --check` and `beats.py codex-doctor` before suggesting repair actions.
Do not run Dotcontext repair, adapter fix, or cleanup flows unless the user explicitly asks for setup or repair.
Report warnings separately from hard failures.
